full_description:
Learn how to create professional, scalable vector graphics using Adobe Illustrator.

This practical Adobe Illustrator — Vector Graphics & Print Design course develops hands-on skills in vector drawing, precision path construction, typography, icon design, illustration and commercial artwork production.

Master essential Illustrator tools including the Pen Tool, Curvature Tool, Pathfinder, Shape Builder, compound paths, clipping masks, Appearance panel and object transformation controls.

Learn to create consistent icon systems, original illustrations, typography-led layouts, custom lettering foundations and reusable vector assets.

Explore professional illustration techniques including gradients, blends, patterns, brushes and symbols.

Discover AI-assisted vector concept development with Adobe Illustrator's Text to Vector Graphic and Generative Shape Fill features, while learning to inspect and refine generated geometry manually.

Build practical production skills in working with multiple artboards, RGB and CMYK color, spot colors, bleeds, PDF exports, SVG exports and linked asset management.

Develop a professional portfolio containing a consistent 12-icon family, an original vector illustration, a typography-led poster and a production-ready multi-artboard commercial artwork package.

Complete the course with organized, editable Illustrator source files and correctly prepared digital and print deliverables.

The programme emphasizes vector precision, visual consistency, professional craftsmanship and reliable client handover.

description: Learn Adobe Illustrator for professional vector graphics, typography, scalable illustration and commercial print design. Build precise, editable artwork using manual vector techniques and responsible AI-assisted workflows.
overview: Adobe Illustrator is the definitive global standard for vector graphics, brand asset creation, scalable illustration and commercial print production. This comprehensive 6-week, 48-hour certification programme provides thorough, studio-grade training in precision Bézier curve drawing, Boolean path operations, typography systems, original illustration, and multi-artboard prepress production. Learners master both time-tested manual vector craftsmanship and cutting-edge Adobe Firefly generative vector tools, graduating with an industry-grade portfolio backed by fully editable .ai master source packages.
why_now: In an omnichannel digital and print economy, visual assets must scale infinitely—from tiny 16px digital UI favicons to massive 40-foot outdoor billboards—without loss of clarity. While AI tools can generate raster concepts, agencies, design studios, and packaging manufacturers require mathematically pure, clean vector geometry with organized paths, global color swatches, and editable typography. This course bridges creative design with technical vector production.

modules.title: Vector Design Foundations
modules.objective: Understand Illustrator's vector environment, document setup, design principles, artwork organization and fundamental drawing tools.
topics: Introduction to Adobe Illustrator: role in commercial design, agency workflows, and vector industry standards
Raster versus vector graphics: mathematical vectors, infinite resolution independence, file-size efficiency, and print scalability
Illustrator interface and custom workspaces: Tools panel, Control bar, Properties panel, and docked studio panels
Document creation and profiles: Print, Web, Art & Illustration, canvas dimensions, orientation, and color modes
Artboards in Illustrator: creating, resizing, duplicating, reordering, and multi-artboard canvas architecture
Units, rulers, and coordinate systems: millimeters, inches, points, pixels, zero-point placement, and mathematical precision
Guides and grids: custom guides, Lock/Hide guides, Make Guides from shapes, Smart Guides alignment, and snap settings
Geometric shape tools: Rectangle, Rounded Rectangle, Ellipse, Polygon, Star, Line Segment, and live shape properties
Fill and stroke mechanics: Fill vs Stroke focus, stroke weights, stroke caps (Butt, Round, Projecting), and joins (Miter, Round, Bevel)
Color fundamentals: RGB additive color vs CMYK subtractive process color, Swatches panel, global colors, global color swatches, and color groups
Basic typography tools: Type Tool, Point Type vs Area Type, font selection, font size, tracking, and leading
Artwork organization: Layers panel, sublayers, layer color coding, grouping objects, locking, hiding, and stacking order
Selection tools: Selection Tool (V) bounding box, Direct Selection Tool (A) anchor manipulation, and Group Selection
Alignment and distribution: Align panel, Align to Selection, Align to Key Object, Align to Artboard, and Distribute Spacing
Object transformation: Transform panel, reference point selection, scaling, rotation, reflection, and Free Transform
Basic Appearance panel: understanding object appearance hierarchy and default graphic styles
Core commercial design principles: visual hierarchy, contrast, balance, alignment, proximity, repetition, and positive/negative space
File saving and preservation: native Illustrator (.ai) format, PDF compatibility, Illustrator Cloud documents, and version history
modules.hands_on_practice: Construct grid-aligned geometric poster foundations; set up multi-artboard working canvases; manage global color palettes that update dynamically across multiple document shapes; balance typographic elements with geometric shapes.

assignment.description: Create a precision geometric vector composition across a defined grid using basic shapes, exact mathematical alignment, stroke/fill styling with global color swatches, typographic hierarchy, and structured layer organization.
deliverables: Master editable Adobe Illustrator (.ai) file with named layers
Defined artboard (210 × 297 mm or 1080 × 1350 px) with guides and margins
Balanced composition utilizing at least 4 geometric shape varieties
Global color swatch palette demonstrating consistent color harmony
High-resolution exported PDF and PNG preview files
Short 200-word design rationale explaining geometric structure and alignment

competencies: Vector document and artboard setup
Mathematical alignment and distribution
Global swatch and color management
Stroke and fill precision
Structured layer hierarchy
modules.assessment_criteria: Geometric accuracy, alignment to grid/key objects, proper global swatch implementation, layer naming clarity, and adherence to design principles.

modules.title: Precision Vector Construction
modules.objective: Master accurate vector construction using paths, curves, Boolean operations, object transformation and professional shape-editing techniques.
topics: Path construction fundamentals: anchor points, direction lines, direction handles, and mathematical Bézier curves
Anchor point anatomy: smooth points (collinear handles), corner points (independent handles), open paths, and closed contours
The Pen Tool mastery: click-and-drag curve drafting, handle extension, maintaining smooth curve tangents, and closing paths
Path editing toolset: Add Anchor Point, Delete Anchor Point, Convert Anchor Point Tool, and anchor point alignment controls
The Curvature Tool: intuitive curve drawing, automatic smooth point generation, and double-clicking to toggle corner points
Anchor point optimization: the 'less is more' vector principle, eliminating redundant points, and avoiding lumpy curves
Shape Builder Tool: interactive click-and-drag merging, Alt/Option-click deletion of overlapping regions, and shape coloring
Pathfinder panel deep dive: Shape Modes (Unite, Minus Front, Intersect, Exclude) and Pathfinder operations (Divide, Trim, Merge, Crop, Outline)
Compound paths: combining multiple open/closed paths into a single object, Non-Zero Winding vs Even-Odd fill rules, and creating cutouts
Compound shapes: creating reversible, editable Boolean combinations using Alt-clicking in the Pathfinder panel
Clipping masks: bounding artwork visibility within container shapes, nested masks, and mask editing modes
Offset Path: creating mathematically parallel outer and inner offset contours for badges, borders, and stickers
Outline Stroke versus Offset Path: converting stroke weight into filled closed vector geometry for clean scaling and production
Expand versus Expand Appearance: expanding live shapes, blend effects, strokes, patterns, and dynamic appearances
Variable Width Tool: creating custom stroke calligraphic profiles, adjusting localized stroke thickness, and saving width profiles
Advanced stroke styling: dashed and dotted lines, dash/gap numerical sequencing, stroke corner joins, and arrowheads
Appearance panel stacking: adding multiple fills and multiple strokes to a single path, opacity blending, and live effect stacking
Object transformation tools: Rotate Tool, Reflect Tool (symmetry axis), Scale Tool, Shear Tool, and Transform Each with randomizing options
Repeat features: Radial Repeat, Grid Repeat, and Mirror Repeat for symmetrical badges, mandalas, and technical pattern layouts
Join and Average commands: bridging open path endpoints, averaging coordinate positions, and Path Simplify for clean geometry
Pixel Preview and optical alignment: aligning vector points to the pixel grid for razor-sharp digital display, and optical balance overrides
Vector geometry quality assurance: diagnosing unclosed paths, stray anchor points, overlapping vector artifacts, and inverted handles
modules.hands_on_practice: Hand-trace intricate technical silhouettes with minimal anchor points; execute Boolean subtractions to cut precise internal holes; build multi-stroke decorative badges using the Appearance panel; construct symmetrical emblems using Reflect and Mirror Repeat.

assignment.description: Construct six preliminary commercial vector icons using manual Pen Tool drawing, Shape Builder Boolean operations, Pathfinder unites/subtractions, Offset Path contours, and strict anchor point optimization on a standardized geometric grid.
deliverables: Six preliminary vector icons constructed on a shared 64 × 64 px or 100 × 100 mm grid
Documented construction grid showing underlying geometric circles and diagonals
Editable vector source file showing clean anchor point placement without point bloat
Demonstration of closed paths, unified shapes, and consistent stroke weights
Exported SVG and PNG previews of all six preliminary icons
Anchor point audit log showing path optimization results

competencies: Pen and Curvature Tool proficiency
Boolean path modeling with Pathfinder & Shape Builder
Compound path and clipping mask management
Appearance panel multi-stroke stacking
Anchor point reduction and curve smoothness
modules.assessment_criteria: Curve smoothness, minimal anchor point count, absence of open path errors, clean Boolean shape merging, and geometric consistency across all icons.

modules.title: Typography & Layout Systems
modules.objective: Develop typography and layout proficiency for vector posters, icon families and commercial visual communication.
topics: Typography in commercial vector design: history, classifications (Serif, Sans-Serif, Slab Serif, Script, Monospaced, Display)
Type anatomy: baseline, x-height, cap height, ascenders, descenders, counters, serifs, and terminal nuances
Font pairing and hierarchy: establishing contrast between header, subheader, body copy, and micro-text callouts
Character panel mastery: font family, font style, font size, proportional leading, optical kerning vs metrics kerning, and tracking
Paragraph panel controls: left/center/right alignment, justification options, hyphens control, space before/after paragraph, and indents
Area Type mechanics: text container bounding, threading text between boxes, auto-sizing text frames, and text wrap around vector objects
Point Type versus Area Type: operational differences, avoiding accidental point-type distortion during object scaling
Type on Path Tool: flowing text along open curves, closed geometric paths, flip options, path alignment (Ascender, Descender, Center, Baseline)
Glyphs panel and OpenType features: stylistic alternates, discretionary ligatures, small caps, fractions, and glyph substitutions
Editable text preservation: retaining live fonts in master files, font substitution warnings, and font package dependencies
Text outlines (Create Outlines): converting fonts to vector paths, appropriate use cases, irreversible consequences, and archiving live copies
Custom lettering foundations: modifying outlined letterforms with the Direct Selection Tool, extending terminals, and custom ligature crafting
Vector poster grid systems: column grids, modular grids, baseline grids, golden ratio proportions, and safe printing margins
Layout dynamics: visual rhythm, intentional reading order (Z-pattern, F-pattern), typographic contrast, and purposeful whitespace
Iconography design systems: defining a master icon design specification sheet (grid, padding, live area, stroke weight family, corner radii)
Visual weight and optical sizing: balancing circular vs square icons, compensating for geometric area differences, and optical centering
Icon styles: outlined/stroke-based icons vs filled/solid-state icons, two-tone styles, and maintaining stylistic unity across a suite
SVG icon export standards: viewBox optimization, responsive scaling, removing unnecessary Illustrator metadata, and web developer handoff
hands_on_tools: Type Tool & Type on Path Tool
modules.hands_on_practice: Design an editorial typographic poster where type is the primary visual hero; manipulate outlined letterforms to create custom brand titles; expand preliminary icon sketches into a unified 12-icon family following strict optical and grid rules.

(Part B) Expand your preliminary icon lab into a comprehensive, cohesive 12-icon design system governed by a unified grid and style sheet.
deliverables: Part A: Master editorial typography poster in editable .ai format (A3 / Tabloid dimensions) with live and outlined copies
Part A: Exported high-resolution print-ready PDF with embedded typography
Part B: Complete 12-icon family presented on a master icon specification sheet
Part B: 12 individual, cleanly optimized SVG exports ready for digital implementation
Master vector source file showing shared bounding boxes, icon grids, and stroke profiles
Design system documentation detailing grid dimensions, stroke rules, and optical corrections

competencies: Advanced typographic formatting and hierarchy
Type on Path and custom lettering customization
Icon design system planning and consistency
Optical weight balancing
Clean SVG icon production
modules.assessment_criteria: Typographic legibility, precision of grid alignment, stylistic harmony across all 12 icons, small-scale icon readability (16px / 24px), and proper text preservation.

modules.title: Illustration & AI-Assisted Vectors
modules.objective: Create original vector illustrations using manual drawing techniques and responsibly selected generative vector tools.
topics: Vector illustration fundamentals: commercial illustration briefs, editorial vs product vs advertising illustration styles
Concept development: moodboard curation, thumbnail sketching, and the sketch-to-vector workflow via Template layers
Shape simplification and visual stylization: reducing complex organic forms into bold, expressive vector silhouettes
Advanced curve rendering: sculpting organic vector contours, multi-segment curves, and smooth directional transitions
Gradients in vector illustration: Linear and Radial gradients, Gradient Annotator tool, color stops, opacity stops, and aspect ratios
Freeform gradients and Gradient Mesh: mesh points, mesh patches, directional mesh lines, and photorealistic vector tonal shading
The Blend Tool: creating smooth color transitions, specified steps for multi-line shading, specified distance, and replacing blend spines
Brushes panel mastery: Calligraphic brushes, Art Brushes (stretching artwork along paths), Pattern Brushes (corner/side tiles), and Scatter Brushes
Custom brush creation: authoring custom vector linework, textured ink strokes, stippling brushes, and non-destructive stroke styling
Pattern design: Pattern Options workspace, tile types (Grid, Brick by Row, Brick by Column, Hex by Column), overlap controls, and seamless repeats
Symbols and component reuse: dynamic symbols, Symbol Sprayer toolset, 9-slice scaling, and managing global vector component libraries
Adobe Firefly vector capabilities: Text to Vector Graphic engine (generating Subjects, Scenes, Icons, and Patterns via prompts)
Generative Shape Fill: using existing vector shapes as bounding geometry to generate detailed contextual vector artwork
Prompt engineering for vector artwork: specifying art styles, color palettes, vector complexity, and preventing semantic drift
AI vector inspection and quality control: diagnosing excess anchor points, tangled paths, open unclosed loops, and hidden raster embeds
Manual refinement of AI vectors: using Simplify Path, deleting phantom geometry, re-drawing warped curves, and recoloring with Global Swatches
Intellectual property, copyright, and Adobe Firefly commercial licensing terms, credit consumption, and client provenance documentation
modules.hands_on_practice: Illustrate a stylized commercial character, scene, or botanical subject from an initial pencil sketch; blend multi-line shading profiles; generate vector concept variations with Firefly; manually reconstruct and optimize generated vector contours to achieve clean studio geometry.

modules.title: Commercial Artwork & Production
modules.objective: Produce commercial multi-artboard artwork and prepare reliable digital and print-ready deliverables.
topics: Commercial advertising and marketing design briefs: interpreting technical specifications, brand standards, and delivery deadlines
Physical print dimensions versus digital screen pixels: ISO A-series (A4, A5), US standard paper sizes, and digital banner formats
Multi-artboard commercial production: coordinating coordinated marketing suites (posters, brochures, flyers, social assets) in one file
Prepress technicalities: trim lines, safe content margins, and 3mm (0.125 in) bleed setup for borderless edge-to-edge printing
Printer marks: trim marks, bleed marks, registration marks, color bars, and page information
Color management for print production: converting RGB to CMYK, gamut warnings, color profile assignment (e.g. Coated FOGRA39, US Web Coated)
Spot colors and process printing: Spot Color swatches, Pantone Matching System (PMS) library awareness, and spot-to-process conversions
Overprint and trapping fundamentals: Overprint Fill, Overprint Stroke, Knockout preview, and avoiding misregistration gaps
Black printing rules: pure 100% K black for crisp text vs Rich Black (C:60 M:40 Y:40 K:100) for deep, saturated background solids
Transparency and Flattening: transparency blend spaces (CMYK vs RGB), Flattener Preview panel, and raster/vector balance controls
Image asset management: Links panel, Linked vs Embedded images, checking effective PPI (minimum 300 PPI for print), and updating missing links
Font management and prepress compliance: checking missing fonts, keeping live text in master files, and outlining type only for final print copies
File packaging (File > Package): automated collection of fonts, linked imagery, color profiles, and generation of packaging report
Digital vector export: Export for Screens workspace, SVG export settings (SVG 1.1 vs SVG Tiny, styling internal CSS vs presentation attributes)
PDF creation for print: Adobe PDF presets (High Quality Print, Press Quality, PDF/X-1a, PDF/X-4), standard compliance, and font embedding
Adobe Acrobat inspection and preflight: verifying separations, checking trim/bleed boxes, measuring ink density, and visual proofing
Professional source-file handover standards: 8 standard logical layer groups, descriptive naming, purging unused swatches and symbols
Client delivery package architecture: organizing 01_Editable_AI, 02_Print_PDF, 03_SVG_Assets, 04_Digital_Previews, 05_Linked_Assets, 06_Documentation
modules.hands_on_practice: Set up multi-artboard commercial campaigns with 3mm bleeds; soft-proof spot colors and Rich Black; package a complete production file with fonts and linked imagery; preflight exported PDF/X files in Adobe Acrobat.

ai_handover_standards.handover_assessment: Every package is evaluated on openability, absence of broken links or missing fonts, layer group organization, and path editability. A flattened PNG or rasterized PDF alone receives zero credit.

vector_quality_standards.vector_craftsmanship: Minimal anchor point counts, smooth Bézier curve tangents, absence of unclosed paths, clean Boolean joins, and optical balance.
vector_quality_standards.design_quality: Visual hierarchy, deliberate typography, modular grid alignment, harmonious color palettes, and balanced positive/negative space.
vector_quality_standards.ai_quality: Rigorous inspection of AI-generated vectors, elimination of path bloat, uncrossing of overlapping contours, and manual artistic override.
vector_quality_standards.production_quality: Exact artboard dimensions, verified 3mm print bleeds, CMYK/spot color separation, Rich Black solid coverage, and clean SVG viewBox scaling.

faq.question: What is Adobe Illustrator — Vector Graphics & Print Design?
faq.answer: Adobe Illustrator — Vector Graphics & Print Design is an intensive 6-week, 48-hour certification programme focused on precision vector drawing, Bézier curve mastery, professional typography, scalable icon systems, custom illustration, and commercial print prepress production. Students learn both traditional manual vector craftsmanship and cutting-edge Adobe Firefly AI vector tools, graduating with an industry-grade portfolio backed by fully editable .ai master source packages.

faq.question: Is this course suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. The programme starts with fundamental concepts in vector mechanics, interface navigation, geometric shape creation, and basic design principles before advancing systematically into advanced Pen Tool drawing, typography systems, vector illustration, and prepress engineering. No prior vector design experience is required.

faq.question: What is the duration and fee?
faq.answer: The course duration is exactly 6 Weeks (48 total learning hours), priced at a transparent institutional fee of ₹6,900 (plus applicable 18% GST). Nova Skills follows a strict Truth in Pricing policy with zero artificial countdown discounts, inflated strike-through pricing, or hidden fees.

faq.question: Will I learn the Pen Tool and Curvature Tool?
faq.answer: Yes. Mastery over the Pen Tool and Curvature Tool is the central technical foundation of Module 02. You will learn to control Bézier handles, draft smooth curve tangents, place anchor points with mathematical efficiency, and construct clean vector paths with minimal anchor points.

faq.question: Does the course cover Pathfinder and Shape Builder?
faq.answer: Yes. Boolean shape operations are covered in depth. You will master both the Pathfinder panel (Unite, Minus Front, Intersect, Exclude, Divide, Trim, Merge) and the interactive Shape Builder Tool to rapidly combine, sculpt, and hollow out complex vector shapes.

faq.question: What is the difference between vector and raster graphics?
faq.answer: Raster graphics (like photos in Photoshop) are composed of a fixed grid of colored pixels that lose quality and become pixelated when enlarged. Vector graphics (in Illustrator) are built from mathematical paths, points, curves, and fills that scale infinitely to any size—from a 16px mobile icon to a 40-foot building billboard—with perfect razor-sharp clarity.

faq.question: Will I learn vector icon design?
faq.answer: Yes. Icon design is taught as a rigorous, systematic discipline in Modules 02 and 03. You will learn to construct icon grids, define stroke families, establish consistent corner radii, optically balance circular vs square masses, and export production-ready SVGs for mobile and web apps.

faq.question: How many icons will I create?
faq.answer: You will create a complete, cohesive family of exactly twelve vector icons. The project begins with a 6-icon precision construction lab in Module 02 and expands into a unified 12-icon design system accompanied by an icon specification sheet in Module 03.

faq.question: Does the course include professional typography?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 03 provides comprehensive training in commercial typography, covering typeface classifications, font pairing, character/paragraph formatting, optical kerning, proportional leading, Area Type vs Point Type, Type on Path, OpenType glyphs, and custom lettering foundations.

faq.question: Will I create an original illustration?
faq.answer: Yes. In Module 04, you will complete an original commercial vector hero illustration from thumbnail sketches to final digital artwork, applying advanced curve rendering, custom gradients, Gradient Mesh, the Blend Tool, and custom vector brushes.

faq.question: Will I learn Text to Vector Graphic?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn how to responsibly deploy Adobe Firefly Text to Vector Graphic inside Illustrator to explore concept variations, generate vector subjects and patterns via prompts, and integrate AI exploration into your creative process without sacrificing manual vector control.

faq.question: Does the course include Generative Shape Fill?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn to use Generative Shape Fill to populate existing vector boundaries with contextually relevant, style-matched vector artwork, while learning how to direct color palettes and complexity levels.

faq.question: Can AI-generated vectors always be edited perfectly?
faq.answer: No, and understanding this limitation is a key learning outcome. Generative AI vectors frequently suffer from anchor point bloat, overlapping path artifacts, unwanted clipping masks, unclosed loops, and hidden raster elements. The course teaches rigorous manual inspection and geometry cleanup to bring AI assets up to commercial production standards.

faq.question: Will I learn print-ready PDF production?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 05 provides thorough prepress training, covering PDF/X standards, bleed settings, trim marks, printer marks, font embedding, transparency flattening, and preflight inspection in Adobe Acrobat to guarantee problem-free commercial printing.

faq.question: Does the course teach SVG export?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn to configure clean SVG exports for digital products and websites, optimizing viewBox coordinates, eliminating unnecessary Illustrator metadata, and ensuring responsive scalability across modern web browsers.

faq.question: What are bleed and trim in print design?
faq.answer: Trim is the final physical cut line where the printed page is trimmed. Bleed is the extra area (typically 3mm or 0.125 inches) extending beyond the trim line where background colors and imagery are deliberately extended, preventing unsightly white paper borders when the guillotine cuts the paper stack.

faq.question: Will I receive editable Illustrator source files?
faq.answer: Yes, and you will be trained to produce and deliver them professionally. Every portfolio project requires native, editable .ai master working files organized across the 8 standard logical layer groups with live text preserved and non-destructive appearances intact.

faq.question: What portfolio projects are included?
faq.answer: You will build four major commercial portfolio projects: (1) Professional Vector Icon System (12-icon family), (2) Commercial Vector Illustration, (3) Editorial Typography Poster, and (4) Print & Digital Production Artwork (multi-artboard commercial campaign with full prepress packaging).

faq.question: Do I need an Adobe Illustrator subscription?
faq.answer: Learners need access to desktop Adobe Illustrator (version 2024 or later recommended) via an active Creative Cloud subscription or trial. Studio laboratory access is provided for classroom students during campus studio hours. Desktop Illustrator is required for full professional toolsets.

faq.question: Are Adobe generative credits included?
faq.answer: Adobe Creative Cloud plans include a monthly allocation of generative credits for Firefly features. The curriculum teaches efficient, prompt-optimized workflows that consume minimal credits, and manual vector drawing alternatives are provided for every AI-assisted technique.

faq.question: Does this course cover complete brand identity strategy?
faq.answer: No. Corporate brand positioning, extensive market research, and multi-touchpoint brand strategy are covered in separate specialized branding pathways. Course 49 focuses specifically on vector craft, icon design, typography, illustration, and commercial print production.

faq.question: Does the course teach professional vector logo research?
faq.answer: While you will learn foundational shape construction and typography essential for logo creation, specialized trademark legal clearance, comprehensive logo identity systems, and brand mark strategy belong to dedicated logo and brand identity courses.

faq.question: How is this course different from Adobe Photoshop?
faq.answer: Adobe Photoshop (Course 48) specializes in raster pixel editing, photo retouching, color grading, photorealistic compositing, and raster advertising banners. Adobe Illustrator (Course 49) specializes in mathematically scalable vector geometry, typography, icon systems, vector illustration, and print prepress.

faq.question: Is this an official Adobe certification?
faq.answer: This course awards the Nova Skills Certified Vector Graphics & Print Specialist (NS-VGPS) credential, an independent institutional qualification certifying practical commercial vector competency. It is not an Adobe Certified Professional (ACP) exam voucher, though the syllabus comprehensively prepares students wishing to sit for ACP exams.

faq.question: What career opportunities are available?
faq.answer: Graduates are qualified for entry-level and junior commercial design roles including Junior Vector Graphic Designer, Adobe Illustrator Designer, Vector Illustration Assistant, Icon Designer, Print Artwork Production Assistant, Advertising Artwork Assistant, Digital Asset Designer, and Freelance Vector Designer.
